prs.title: [CI] Relax sharded-sampling divergence bound on ROCm
prs.author: khluu
prs.body_head:
## Purpose

`tests/v1/e2e/general/test_sharded_sampling.py::test_sharded_sampling_outputs_match` asserts that batch-sharded sampling matches the replicated fallback up to near-tie boot-state noise, allowing at most `MAX_DIVERGENT_PROMPTS = 3` of 16 prompts to diverge. That bound was tuned on CUDA (measured ≤ 1 divergent prompt per engine boot).

On ROCm/MI300 the engine boots land in noisier kernel/collective states, and the test flakes at **4–7 divergent prompts** — above the CUDA bound but still far below the near-total divergence a real request-misrouting bug produces. In a scan of the last 200 CI builds, this single test accounted for **11 flaky failures**, all on `:amd: (MI300) Distributed DP Basic`, with divergence of 4/16, 5/16, 6/16, and 7/16.

This PR raises the divergence bound to `8` on ROCm only; CUDA keeps the tight bound of `3`. A genuine sharding bug (rows routed to the wrong request, misaligned gathers) still fails, since it diverges on nearly every prompt.

## Why this is not a duplicate

Checked open PRs/issues for `sharded_sampling`, `test_sharded_sampling`, and `prompts diverged`; no existing PR addresses this flake.

## Test plan / commands run

- Flake evidence: analyzed the public Buildkite `ci` pipeline's last 200 builds via the `/data/jobs` endpoint; extracted 240 "failed-then-passed-on-retry" jobs and read each failing attempt's log. 11 were this test, all AMD MI300, divergence 4–7/16 (data and method in the linked tracking issue).
- `pre-commit run` passes (ruff, mypy, etc.) on the changed file.
- This is a numerical-tolerance change to a distributed GPU test; I could not run the full 2-GPU test locally (no multi-GPU box). The ROCm path is exercised by the `:amd: (MI300) Distributed DP Basic` CI job.

## AI assistance

This change was developed with AI assistance (Kimi Code), including the CI log analysis that identified the flake.

prs.title: [CI] Reclaim GPU memory between model initialization tests
prs.author: khluu
prs.body_head:
## Summary

Deflake the model-initialization tests in `tests/models/test_initialization.py` by reclaiming GPU memory between tests.

### Flaky tests addressed

From a Buildkite flaky-test analysis (suite `ci-1`):

| Test | Reliability | Failed/Total |
|---|---|---|
| `test_can_initialize_small_subset[InternVLChatModel]` | 0.998 | 8/3288 |

Buildkite: https://buildkite.com/organizations/vllm/analytics/suites/ci-1/tests/b1f1fe69-2515-83bb-bbd3-b15a219bbdce

The same failure mode plausibly affects the sibling tests in this module (`test_can_initialize_large_subset`, e.g. `Step3TextForCausalLM` 5/1072, `Step3VLForConditionalGeneration` 5/1050, `Gemma4MTPModel` 3/1050), which run at the same `gpu_memory_utilization=0.80`.

### Root cause

Each parametrized case in this module builds a full vLLM `LLM` in a fresh subprocess via `create_new_process_for_each_test()` with `gpu_memory_utilization=0.80` — the source itself carries the comment "these tests seem to produce leftover memory". On NVIDIA the subprocess is **forked**, and its VRAM is only reclaimed asynchronously by the driver when the subprocess exits. The next test can start (and allocate ~80% of the GPU, e.g. an 18 GiB H200 MIG slice) before that reclamation completes, so leftover memory from a preceding test OOMs a later one — consistent with the observed ~0.24% failure rate hitting the heavier multimodal archs like InternVLChatModel. Prior art: b6770d7b (#48527) hit OOM in this exact test on ROCm.

### What changed

Added a module-level autouse fixture `cleanup_gpu_memory_between_tests` that runs after each test:

1. `gc.collect()` + `torch.accelerator.empty_cache()`
2. Wait (via NVML, using the existing `wait_for_gpu_memory_to_clear` / `wait_for_memory_to_settle` helpers from `tests/utils.py`) for the forked subprocess's VRAM to actually clear before the next test runs. A wait timeout is logged, not raised, so it can never fail a test.
